title: Review a Dockerfile before it ships

blocks.text: The roster team builds its own images, and the platform team wants a check in CI that refuses a Dockerfile breaking the four rules every image on the cluster must follow. Write it.
In `dockerfile_review.py`, write `review(dockerfile)`. It takes a Dockerfile's text and returns the sorted list of findings, each at most once:

rows: a `FROM` image has no tag, or the tag `latest`, and no `@sha256:` digest. A `FROM` that names an earlier stage (`FROM build`, after `FROM ... AS build`) is not a base image. The colon of a registry port (`host:5000/python`) is not a tag. `FROM scratch` (in any case) names Docker's reserved empty image, which has no tag to pin, so it is never flagged.
the **final** stage has no `USER`, or its last `USER` is `root` or `0` (a `user:group` form counts by its user part). Every stage starts as root: a `USER` in an earlier stage does not carry over.
an `ENV` or `ARG` sets a variable whose name, in upper case, contains `KEY`, `SECRET`, `TOKEN` or `PASSWORD`. An `ENV` line may set several `NAME=value` pairs.
a `CMD` or `ENTRYPOINT` is not in exec form (does not start with `[`).

blocks.text: Instruction words may be written in any case. `instructions(dockerfile)` is given: it drops comments and blank lines and returns `(WORD, rest)` pairs with the word in upper case. You may assume one instruction per line. About 25 lines remain.

cases.says: a clean two-stage file has no findings, and a file breaking all four rules has all four
a base tagged latest is not pinned; a base pinned by sha256 digest is
the port in a registry host name is not mistaken for a tag
FROM scratch names Docker's empty image, which has no tag to pin, so it is not flagged
a USER in the build stage does not make the final stage non-root
USER 0 and USER root:root still run as root
a password among several ENV pairs, in lower case, is found
a lower-case shell-form entrypoint is a shell-form command

origin.section: The Image Runs as a Non-Root User and Holds No Credentials

concepts: a non-root user, a build context filter and no credentials baked in
one image serves the API and the solve worker under two commands in exec form
